standardOnBackground  Checked by plugin
Use frames to create a component

Always use frames to create components

Rectangles and other shapes should only be used for visual elements that don’t contain content.



When to use shapes example

The progress indicator in the loading spinner consists of visual elements without additional content. Therefore, they can be built with shapes.



savings  Mandatory rule
standardOnBackground  Checked by plugin
Apply auto-layout to frames

Always apply auto-layout to frames containing sublayers

Use auto-layout to adjust the frame layout (horizontal, vertical, or wrap).
Add spacing between frames as needed.
Include padding for the frame if required.
Select the variables for spacing/components from the One ID Foundation Library, otherwise leave the value as 0.



When not to apply auto-layout to frames

Don’t apply auto-layout to frames that do not contain any sublayers.


For example, in the Switch component, the ‘Container’ frame has auto-layout since it has the ‘Stroke’ and ‘Handle’ sublayers inside it. But the ‘Stroke’ and ‘Handle’ frames do not since they have no sublayers.



savings  Mandatory rule
Component variants structure

When creating variants of a component, keep the same structure among them.


If a layer is not needed in a variant, it should be present in the structure and hidden.


You should lock any hidden layers that should not appear on one variant, but should on another.



savings  Mandatory rule
standardOnBackground  Checked by plugin
Component instance overrides

Component instances can only have frame dimension overrides, and only on the outer, component instance frame.

Width / Height
Min / Max dimensions
Horizontal / Vertical resizing(Fill,Hug, Fix)

Please note, you can override dimensions on an instance used within a component, but you cannot override other instances contained within that instance.



warning  Best practice
Keep the component structure simple

Ensure each layer you use is necessary.


Avoid adding layers solely for visual styling, such as background layers for color or borders, as this can cause code issues.



warning  Best practice
Use existing components to build complex ones

Utilize existing ODS basic components as building blocks for creating more complex components.


If any necessary components are missing, contact the ODS team to discuss whether to build them yourself or have them provided.
